Each customer from the **customers** and **orders** records has been scored 1–5 across three dimensions. A score of **5 = best** for Frequency and Monetary; for Recency, **5 = most recent** (fewest days since last order), **1 = most lapsed**.

All three scores are evenly distributed across quintiles (avg = 2.97 each), confirming a well-balanced segmentation.

## Customer Spending Quintiles

93 customers are segmented into 5 quintiles (18–19 customers each), generating a combined **EUR 448,386,633** in total revenue.

| Quintile | Customers | Total Revenue (EUR) | Avg Rev / Customer (EUR) | % of Total |
|----------|-----------|--------------------:|-------------------------:|----------:|
| 1 (Top) | 19 | 103,443,611 | 5,444,401 | 23.07% |
| 2 | 19 | 94,209,464 | 4,958,393 | 21.01% |
| 3 | 19 | 90,871,497 | 4,782,710 | 20.27% |
| 4 | 18 | 82,871,898 | 4,604,000 | 18.48% |
| 5 (Bottom) | 18 | 76,990,163 | 4,277,231 | 17.17% |

### Key Takeaways

- **Revenue is relatively balanced** across quintiles — the top quintile accounts for 23.07% vs. 17.17% for the bottom, a spread of only ~6 percentage points. This suggests no extreme concentration of revenue in a small customer group.
- **Top quintile customers generate ~35% more revenue on average** than bottom quintile customers (EUR 5.4M vs. EUR 4.3M per customer), indicating meaningful but not dramatic differentiation.
- **Quintiles 4 and 5 (36 customers)** represent EUR 159.9M — nearly 36% of total revenue — and warrant retention focus to prevent revenue erosion.

### Recommendation
Prioritize loyalty and upsell programs for Quintiles 1–2 while deploying targeted engagement campaigns for Quintiles 4–5 to migrate mid-to-low spenders upward.
